event.title: Your First Pull Request
event.text: Your tech lead left 52 comments on your first PR. Half are nitpicks about whitespace. You're not sure if this is normal or a sign you should quit.

left.text: Rewrite the whole thing from scratch.

right.text: Address the key comments and ship it.

event.title: Imposter Syndrome
event.text: A senior asks you to present your first feature to the whole engineering team. Your code works, but you're convinced everyone will see through you.

left.text: Say you're sick. Present next time.

right.text: Do the presentation. Face the fear.

event.title: Unassigned Friday
event.text: Your senior is in back-to-back meetings and forgot to give you tasks. The backlog is huge but you're not sure you're allowed to just pick things up.

left.text: Self-assign a backlog ticket and go.

right.text: Browse docs and learn something new.

event.title: Stuck for Three Hours
event.text: You've been staring at the same bug for three hours. You could ask a colleague, but you don't want to seem incompetent on your second week.

right.text: Ask for help. That's what seniors are for.

event.title: You Broke Production
event.text: Your deploy went out and something unrelated stopped working. The logs are a maze. Nobody noticed yet — but it's only a matter of time.

left.text: Ask for help immediately, own it.

right.text: Debug in silence and fix it before anyone sees.

event.title: Speak Up in the Meeting
event.text: The team is debating a database schema choice. You have a strong opinion from a side project — but nobody asked, and the seniors seem decided.

right.text: Share your perspective. Politely.

event.title: New Intern Assigned to You
event.text: HR just assigned you a new intern to mentor. You barely feel settled yourself. They're asking questions every 20 minutes.

left.text: Dedicate real time to mentoring them.

right.text: Point them to the docs and focus on your work.

event.title: Tech Debt Reckoning
event.text: The team is drowning in legacy code. Your senior dev insists the next sprint must be a full refactor — no features, just cleanup.

right.text: Schedule the refactor sprint.

event.title: Meeting Culture
event.text: Standups have crept to 45 minutes. One engineer says they're the only alignment we have. Another says they destroy deep work time.

right.text: 15-minute cap, async updates for the rest.

event.title: Review Policy
event.text: After a costly regression, your TL proposes mandatory two-person code reviews on all PRs. Junior devs love it. Senior devs call it a bottleneck.

right.text: Trust the team. Optional reviews.

event.title: Shiny New Stack
event.text: An architect proposes rewriting the diagnostics service in a trendy new framework. Faster long-term, but six months of migration pain first.

right.text: Keep the legacy service. It works.

event.title: Talent Gap
event.text: A project deadline looms and the team lacks bandwidth. HR proposes hiring an expensive contractor to plug the gap immediately.

right.text: Push the team harder.

event.title: Security Audit Findings
event.text: A third-party audit uncovered three high-severity vulnerabilities in the OTA update system. Fixing them means halting feature work for two weeks.

right.text: Patch the worst one, defer the rest.

event.title: On-Call Roulette
event.text: Three engineers are bearing the entire on-call load. They want a fair rotation. The rest of the team is nervous — they don't know the system well enough.

right.text: Keep the specialists on-call.

event.title: Customer Shortcut
event.text: Your biggest client asks for a "temporary" hardcoded config flag to bypass the validation pipeline. They need it by Friday or they walk.

left.text: Add the flag. Keep the client.

right.text: Offer a proper solution in three weeks.

event.title: Observability Investment
event.text: The ops team says without proper monitoring, the next incident will take days to diagnose. Setup takes a sprint. The roadmap is already packed.

right.text: Add it to the backlog. Ship the roadmap.

event.title: Team Offsite Proposal
event.text: The people team wants to organise a two-day offsite at a mountain retreat to boost morale after a tough quarter. It's not cheap.

right.text: Virtual coffee chat will do.

event.title: Deadline Crunch
event.text: The board pushed the product demo date forward by three weeks. Your PM says mandatory weekends will make it. Your team lead looks exhausted.

right.text: Negotiate scope. Protect the team.

event.title: Open Source vs In-House
event.text: Your team wants to use an open-source CAN bus parsing library. Legal flags it as a potential IP risk. Building in-house takes two months.

left.text: Use the open-source library. Ship faster.

right.text: Build it in-house. Control the IP.

event.title: Production Is on Fire
event.text: A critical bug has hit the vehicle telemetry pipeline. Engineers want to push a quick hotfix now. QA says wait for a proper review cycle.

right.text: Wait for proper QA.

event.title: The Docs Are a Desert
event.text: New hires are struggling to onboard because almost nothing is documented. Someone proposes a quarterly "docs day" — no feature work, just writing.

left.text: Dedicate a full day every quarter.

right.text: Docs happen organically. Back to coding.

event.title: Return to Office Memo
event.text: Leadership wants three days in-office per week. Half the team is remote and moved cities. Some say it'll help collaboration. Others say they'll quit.

right.text: Stay fully flexible. Async-first culture.
